text:
ash: seeing spike in local NVMe write latency on gnode-pool-7, GPU provisioning requests are timing out and jobs queueing up. :warning:
ash: example tail from node gnode-7b:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:33Z] nvme0n1: write_latency=12.4ms iops=18k queue_depth=128
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] nvme0n1: scrub_worker=active io_wait=45%
```
devon: noted, I saw similar in metrics last night — scrub backlog + heavy batch checkpointing. Could be cleaner/GC stomping IO.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-032 (nvme-iops-surge) — paging eng-oncall.
maria: can we throttle the scrubber and slow background GC for the next 30m? That usually buys time for provisioning.
ash: +1. what's the knob? I know we exposed `ephemeral.scrub_rate` in node config but not sure the default on this pool.
maria: config patch suggestion:
```yaml
ephemeral:
  scrub_rate: 0.25  # reduce to 25% of normal
  max_concurrent_scrubs: 1
```
maria: this should reduce background IO by ~60-70% in our tests.
sam: we can also push low-priority batch jobs to standby-pool-2 for 2hrs. Less churn on gnode-pool-7 while scrub is throttled. Want me to flip job routing?
devon: yes flip. Also check SMART on nodes — if wear is high we should cordon before it turns into corruptions. run: `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` and grep for Wear_Leveling_Count.
ash: ran SMART on gnode-7b, wear level ~ 72% remaining, no reallocated sectors yet. So not immediate fail but headroom is shrinking.
maria: ops decision options: (1) throttle scrubs + move batch jobs (low cost, immediate), (2) cordon high-wear nodes and reprovision from spare pool (medium cost), (3) schedule drive replacement/rotate hardware (higher capital + ETA 2-3w).
sam: preference 1 then 2 if no improvement in 1-3 hours. I'll start moving job routing now.
ash: doing scrub throttle patch now, rolling update across gnode-pool-7 with one-per-zone to avoid mass churn.
ash: patch applied to 3/6 nodes so far — seeing immediate drop in write latency to ~3.2ms. provisioning success rate improving. :thumbsup:
devon: can we add a short-term autoscale tweak to prefer nodes with write_latency <5ms for GPU scheduling? Might help scheduling logic until we fix fleet.
maria: yep I can add a routing rule: `prefer: write_latency < 5ms` for 1 hour window. I'll push that.
ops-bot: INC-2026-032 updated: mitigation in progress (scrub throttle + routing changes).
ash: next steps: monitor for 3h, if latency creeps back we cordon high-wear nodes and shift workloads. Also need a postmortem: root cause (scrub+checkpoint overlap) + cost tradeoff (replace drives vs tune heuristics).
sam: noting cost: temporary routing + throttles = near zero. Replacing 20 drives in region-eu-west would be ~ $30k + logistics. Will draft cost note for infra leads.
maria: thanks. I'll keep watch and post metrics link: https://internal.metrics/gnode-pool-7/2026-03-15
devon: adding runbook step to avoid simultaneous full checkpoints during scrub windows. small change but avoids recurrence.
ash: great, closing thread if stable after 3h. If anyone sees provisioning errors ping here.
